terms.gloss: a manager, the agent who runs things for the owner
evidence: Cic. Caecin. 57: prōcūrātor, aliēnī jūris vicārius (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The owner’s manager or agent (Lewis & Short); on a farm the vīlicus worked under him.

terms.gloss: the manager of a farm or estate; a foreman

evidence: Traupman 276: argentāriae moderātor, a bank manager
Cic. N.D. 2.90: rēctor et moderātor tantī operis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Traupman’s word for a manager; a woman is moderātrīx.

phrases.latin: vīlicum vocet, roget quid operis siet factum, quid restet
phrases.english: let him call in his manager and ask what work has been done and what remains

phrases.latin: sī mandandum aliquid prōcūrātōrī … aut imperandum vīlicō est
phrases.english: if some instruction has to be given to the manager … or an order to the foreman

sources: Lewis & Short: procurator · Lewis & Short: vilicus · Lewis & Short: moderator
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 276, 318, 330, 343.
